A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LED research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, layerwise entropy measurements, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and a reasoning case study.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original GRPO training experiments and hardware latency/throughput measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix D.3 extend LED into GRPO rollout generation, a limited adaptation of the training procedure. LED's filtering, cumulative aggregation, entropy selection, confidence gating, and DeepThink-only decoding remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 newly uses filtered MATH-lighteval problems for original GRPO training and held-out evaluation, extending data usage within mathematics beyond v2's MATH-500 evaluation. All six original mathematics, science, and coding benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: New Table 4 introduces regular-rollout GRPO training and untrained-model controls for the training comparison. Existing accuracy comparisons retain CoT, DoLa, SoftThinking, and SoftThinking-Gumbel; the new efficiency comparisons evaluate Regular, DoLa, and SoftThinking.

E3.justification: v3 adds a GRPO experiment with approximately 750 training and 750 test problems, crossing training rollout strategy with evaluation decoder. It also introduces latency tests at batch size 4 with 8K/16K contexts on eight A100s, and throughput tests at batch size 128 with 16K contexts on eight H100s. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Figures 9–10 add training-reward and before/after validation analyses, while Appendix E investigates runtime components and high-concurrency efficiency. These substantially expand analysis into learning dynamics and computational costs. Earlier component ablations, depth sensitivity, entropy analyses, and case-study findings remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 16-attempt pass@1 averaging and the seed-0 disclosure. v3 adds no repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; its smoothed training curves do not establish uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds training and runtime results. Table 4 reports 43.10 versus 41.99 accuracy under Regular evaluation after LED versus Regular rollout training, and 45.44 when LED is used for both. Table 8 reports 4204 versus 4578 tokens/s for LED versus Regular. Original benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, including renumbered appendix tables.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, LED's complexity analysis, and Appendix B's GRPO/entropy reasoning are retained. The new training experiment introduces no revised mathematical objective, formal assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list newly claim that LED rollouts produce faster reward improvement and better final GRPO performance. This materially extends the central contribution into improving training, while retaining the original entropy-collapse and inference-accuracy claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the cross-decoder results as improvements to the learned policy and attributes reduced training time to shorter rollouts. Appendix E adds an accuracy-efficiency interpretation and attributes added decoding overhead mainly to the LM head. Existing entropy-mechanism explanations and QwQ failure discussion remain.

D1.justification: New appendices disclose VeRL/SGLang use, the filtered training-data identifier, H100/A100 hardware, timing configurations, and training durations. The project link also changes its repository address. The original executable LED listing and inference implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4.4 extends LED's positioning from post-training decoding correction to supporting GRPO through rollout generation. The cited-work membership and Appendix A's comparisons with earlier research remain unchanged; the GPQA reference update is bibliographic only.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the case-study explanation, inserts the rollout section and new appendices, and adjusts subsequent section numbering. It also updates affiliation/publication text and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: New Table 4, Figures 9–10, and Tables 7–8 substantially expand the visual evidence for training and efficiency. Existing figures are resized or repositioned with their content retained, and old Tables 4–5 become Tables 5–6. Figure 7's shortened caption loses its model identification and baseline explanation.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a useful cross-decoder control for the GRPO extension and direct hardware measurements beyond v2's complexity and generation-length evidence. The gains are limited by a single filtered mathematics training setup without reported training-run uncertainty. Also, Table 7 does not consistently support the new attribution of added latency mainly to the LM head. Overall empirical support improves while the original results remain intact.
